scope: six officially mapped parking assets crosschecked to named DNR recreation points, without a certified signed pedestrian entrance or passable path
safetyPolicy: A GIS point match, guide instruction, photo, or nearby line does not establish a legal walking route, an open bridge, or an accessible trail.

records.separationMeaning: Straight-line offset between DNR GIS parking and named-recreation points; not walking distance, turn, trail length or proof of connection
records.relation: DNR guide describes an approximately 100-yard paved or boardwalk scenic overlook approach from the scenic-area parking.
records.nextAction: If the M-107 scenic road and lot are open, follow the signed overlook path. The Escarpment wilderness trail is not that short boardwalk.

records.separationMeaning: Straight-line offset between DNR GIS parking and named-recreation points; not walking distance, turn, trail length or proof of connection
records.relation: The DNR describes a half-mile packed-dirt path from Summit Peak scenic parking to the tower stairs.
records.nextAction: Find the posted Summit Peak Tower Trail start on site. The upper lot and unverified camper/trailer staging should not be confused.

records.separationMeaning: Straight-line offset between DNR GIS parking and named-recreation points; not walking distance, turn, trail length or proof of connection
records.relation: The DNR's named East/West River recreation point is matched to a trail-area parking feature, but no verified route connects this GIS point to the day-use area, contact booth, gravel Nawadaha path, or bridge.
records.nextAction: Verify the current County Road 519 access and follow posted day-use/waterfall signage. Do not presume the contact-booth path starts at DNR asset #841.

records.relation: DNR matches the Visitor Center Nature Trail recreation point and nearby parking; it describes a 1.4-mile loop but our linework does not independently identify its signed entry.
records.nextAction: Look for signed Nature Trail guidance near the Visitor Center, and verify outdoor access separately from building hours.

records.separationMeaning: Straight-line offset between DNR GIS parking and named-recreation points; not walking distance, turn, trail length or proof of connection
records.relation: The easy Lake of the Clouds overlook and long Escarpment Trail share a mapped parking district, not an established same-path start or return. Official editions conflict on trail mileage.
records.nextAction: Locate the actual ridge-trail start/end on the DNR map and arrange return/shuttle plans. Do not follow the short boardwalk as a guaranteed ridge-trail connection.

records.relation: The DNR ski-area parking feature aligns with a named Triple Trail recreation point; it is not independent proof of a modern lodge entrance, lift loading, rental desk, or groomed ski-trail start.
records.nextAction: Approach from the east by M-64 in winter, check the official ski report and look for signed parking; don't infer access from the Triple Trail GIS point.
